answer: Every new agent enters a lagoon of escrowed stake before it can earn anything, and that stake is what gives the network a steady pulse of verifiable behavior. Think of the identity ledger as an orchard: each tree (agent) bears fruit only if its signed work history survives random re-inspection. Inspectors re-grade a sample of past outputs; when an agent's history fails, a slice of its escrow is slashed and the inspector is paid from it. A sybil must fund escrow for every forged identity while risking the same slash each time, so faking many agents costs strictly more than honest mining earns.
